samir (customer): Hey team — after the model flip yesterday some of our embedding lookups are failing. We see a few different behaviours: 
- some queries return a 400 with "dimension mismatch" when we try to rehydrate cached vectors
- other queries return an embedding that unhelpfully has the wrong dimension (1536 instead of 1024) 
- throughput dropped because we fell back to regenerating embeddings a lot, billing spiked.

maya (support): Thanks Samir — can you share a request id or an example input we can use to repro? Also which model did you switch from/to?

samir (customer): Request id: r-0a1b2c3d. We were on open-embed-1024-v1 -> switched to open-embed-lite-1536-v2 last night. We use a cache prefix header in our app: `X-EMB-PREFIX: team-metrics`. We're intentionally reusing the same prefix across multiple models to keep it simple.

ashwin (eng-ml): quick note: reusing a shared prefix across models can be fine if your cache key includes model id + dimension. Does your code include model in the key?

samir (customer): I thought the service would namespace keys by model automatically. Our client-side code just uses `prefix + text` as the cache key and relies on the server cache for separation. Example JS: 
```js
const key = `${prefix}:${text}`;
await cache.set(key, embedding);
```
We didn't add model/version to that string.

lina (eng-runtime): @ashwin @maya interesting — looking at the runtime logs for r-0a1b2c3d shows cache reads returning vectors of length 1536 but the active model expected 1024 for some requests. Two likely causes: (1) our cache key derivation previously didn't always include the exact model variant in a few older runtime versions, (2) there was a staggered rollout where some nodes were still serving old model variants and wrote incompatible vectors under the same prefix.

maya (support): That matches what Samir reported — some vectors rehydrated OK, others rejected with dimension mismatch. Can you paste the raw failure snippet?

samir (customer): Sure — here's the embed error we get on the client when rehydration fails: 
```
{
  "error": "embedding dimension mismatch",
  "expected": 1024,
  "received": 1536,
  "cache_key": "team-metrics:How do I reset my password?"
}
```

ashwin (eng-ml): Hmm. So the cache key Samir used lacks model info. On some runtime versions (pre-2026-03-01), the cache key format was simply `prefix + text` unless the customer explicitly opted into `includeModelInKey`. After the rollout, we fixed defaulting to include model/version, but there was a window where previously written keys remain in cache. If a newer node later reads the old key, it doesn't always detect mismatch until rehydration — leading to both silent replacements and explicit errors.

lina (eng-runtime): Repro steps for us (internal):
1) Start a dedicated dev cluster pinned to `open-embed-1024-v1`.
2) Write vectors with prefix `team-metrics` for some sample texts.
3) Roll the cluster to `open-embed-lite-1536-v2` without flushing cache.
4) Issue reads using the same prefix. You'll see a mixed set of returns: some nodes still read old keys; others attempt to reformat and fail.

maya (support): Samir, for a quick mitigation you can either: (a) rotate your prefix immediately (append a short version tag, e.g., `team-metrics-v2`), or (b) change client keying to include model+version (`prefix:model:hash(text)`). That will avoid reusing stale keys.

samir (customer): We can rotate the prefix, but we have ~200k items. Any guidance on doing that without causing a huge regen cost?

ashwin (eng-ml): Two options: incremental migration or on-demand rekeying.
- Incremental: write a small migration job that reads old keys, verifies dimension, and writes new keys keyed by `prefix:model:...` — run in batches. This avoids regenerating embeddings if the cached vector is compatible.
- On-demand: change client to use new key format so future reads look up new keys, and keep old keys in cache to be lazily invalidated. The downside is increased misses until objects are repopulated.

lina (eng-runtime): Also adding: our current runtime will log a metric `cache.dimension_mismatch` and increment a counter when rehydration fails. We've surfaced the request ids for Samir's tenant to detect all impacted items and will perform a targeted flush of stale keys if you want.

samir (customer): Targeted flush would be great. We want to avoid regenerating everything. Also can you explain why we saw throughput drop — even malformed reads seemed to add latency?

lina (eng-runtime): When a cache miss occurs we do a synchronous regenerate which adds CPU/GPU work. But when rehydration returns a wrong-dimension vector, the node attempts validation and then falls back to regenerating, which can serialise across the batching layer causing head-of-line blocking for other requests in the same batch. In practice that shows up as higher p95 latency and more small GPU jobs.

maya (support): Action items: 
- Lina: run the targeted flush for tenant samir-corp and confirm counters before/after (assigned).
- Ashwin: schedule a short runtime patch that enforces including explicit model/version in cache key derivation on all nodes (backfill safe).
- Samir: consider rotating your prefix or updating client keying; we can assist with a migration script.

ops-bot: NOTE: ticket #INC-2026-311 created for cache namespace incident; paging oncall.

samir (customer): Thanks — appreciated. We'll start prefix rotation and will coordinate migration. Any ETA on the runtime patch?

ashwin (eng-ml): I can ship a hotfix to force model-in-key within 6 hours; roll will be canaryed then promoted. We'll post the rollout plan in #eng-runtime. Expect reduced mismatches after propagation.

maya (support): I'll keep this thread updated. If you can send the list of most frequent keys (we can accept a sample) we can prioritize the targeted flush. :thumbsup:

samir (customer): Sending sample list to your DMs now. Thanks all!
